witnesses.provenance: Solana's per-transaction MAX_COMPUTE_UNIT_LIMIT is 1,400,000 compute units. It is the chain's limit, not ours. The campaign sets ProgramTest's ceiling to exactly that value and never raises it.

Solana's legacy packet maximum is 1,232 bytes (PACKET_DATA_BYTES). ProgramTest submits no packet and cannot enforce it, so a frame past the limit survives a fast lane untouched -- Found31 was ten bytes over and survived every fixture test in the tree. DCLLBX02's 28-account frame does not fit a legacy message at all, so every transaction here rides a live v0 Address Lookup Table; this witness serialises what was actually submitted and checks the largest against Solana's stated limit.
A `wire_bytes` of null says the campaign did not measure, which is honest but is not a claim that the frame fits. This asserts that no transaction in this campaign is unmeasured.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.error != null) | select([.logs[] | select(contains("custom program error: 0x"))] | length == 0)] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: The Solana runtime reports a privilege, frame, or account refusal it decides ITSELF as a bare InstructionError with no `custom program error:` log line; that line appears only when a program returned ProgramError::Custom. Every refusal this campaign claims -- named or unnamed_refusal -- is a program decision, so a bare runtime refusal appearing here would mean a hostile case stopped being about a program. It matters more here than in most campaigns, because half of this campaign's rows ARE refusals.

witnesses.query:
.transactions[] | select(.label == "claims liability-basis lifecycle: the composed external-debit split refuses at Custody") | [.logs[] | select(test("^Program [1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]+ failed: custom program error: 0x0$")) | capture("^Program (?

[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]+) failed").p] | first
witnesses.provenance: The load-bearing claim of this campaign is that DCLLBX02's split is refused BY CUSTODY, not by a stale fixture: `expected_custody_request_v2` composes `source_compartment: External` for a split, and `execute_transfer` refuses `CompartmentV1::External` at its head since 84b1426. A campaign asserting that is worthless if Claims raised code 0 on its own. Two independent files answer here: the evidence names the FIRST program in the log to raise 0x0 (Claims re-raises it afterwards, which is propagation, not a decision), and programs.json says which address this campaign pinned as Custody. Neither reads the other.

witnesses.query: .transactions[] | select(.label == "claims liability-basis terminal: the retired TerminalRedeem tag refuses") | [.logs[] | select(test("invoke \\["))] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: `LiabilityBasisActionKindV2::decode` refuses the retired tag on the wire byte, so the refusal happens at decode -- before any account is read, any record authenticated, or any CPI issued. One `invoke [` line is the top-level Claims invocation and nothing else. A refusal arriving later (a Registry read, a Custody composition) would be the same code for a different reason, and would show a second invoke line here.

witnesses.query: .transactions[] | select(.label == "claims liability-basis lifecycle: caller refuses after a complete merge") | (if .error == null then "committed" else ([.logs[] | select(. == "Program TokenkegQfeZyiNwAJbNbGKPFXCWuBvf9Ss623VQ5DA success")] | length | tostring) end)
witnesses.provenance: A rollback case is only evidence if the thing being rolled back actually happened. TokenkegQfeZyiNwAJbNbGKPFXCWuBvf9Ss623VQ5DA is Solana's real, deployed SPL Token program address -- provenance outside this repository entirely. This asserts, from the runtime's own log, that a transaction the ledger records as FAILED contains a COMPLETED token transfer, so the byte-identical prestate the campaign asserts afterwards is a rollback across two CPI boundaries rather than a transaction that never got anywhere. The `if .error == null then "committed"` guard makes a campaign that accidentally let the wrapper commit fail this witness rather than pass it.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.error == null) | select(.label | test("canonical merge commits|unwinds the aggregate to zero")) | .logs[] | select(. == "Program TokenkegQfeZyiNwAJbNbGKPFXCWuBvf9Ss623VQ5DA success")] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: With the split retired at the Custody boundary, the merge is the only DCLLBX02 action that executes at all, and the campaign's whole positive lifecycle is two of them. This counts real SPL Token successes inside transactions the runtime itself recorded as committed -- one Hoard-to-external transfer each -- so a campaign that stopped reaching Custody, or that reached it without moving collateral, fails here rather than passing on its own assertions.
